name: device_prepare
prose: Precondition: dev points to a valid struct device and state describes the system PM transition. Postcondition: the function first takes a runtime PM usage reference with pm_runtime_get_noresume(dev) and calls pm_runtime_block_if_disabled(dev); the local smart_suspend flag starts as true only when that call returned false. If dev->power.syscore is set it returns 0 at that point, before device_lock, without clearing wakeup_path, running any callback, calling device_prepare_smart_suspend, or assigning dev->power.smart_suspend or dev->power.direct_complete, leaving the usage reference held (and any runtime PM block that pm_runtime_block_if_disabled applied). Otherwise it locks dev, clears dev->power.wakeup_path, and unless dev->power.no_pm_callbacks is set picks callback as the first non-empty of: dev->pm_domain->ops.prepare (when pm_domain is set), dev->type->pm->prepare, dev->class->pm->prepare, dev->bus->pm->prepare (each only if the owner and its pm pointer are set, taken in that else-if order), and if callback is still NULL and dev->driver and dev->driver->pm are set, dev->driver->pm->prepare; it calls the callback if non-NULL and then unlocks dev. If the callback returned a negative value, it calls suspend_report_result, pm_runtime_unblock(dev), pm_runtime_put(dev) and returns that negative value without assigning smart_suspend or direct_complete. Otherwise, if the local smart_suspend flag is true it is replaced by device_prepare_smart_suspend(dev); then under dev->power.lock (spin_lock_irq) it assigns dev->power.smart_suspend from that flag, and assigns dev->power.direct_complete to true when state.event is PM_EVENT_SUSPEND, (the callback returned a positive value or dev->power.no_pm_callbacks is set) and DPM_FLAG_NO_DIRECT_COMPLETE is not set for the device, and to false otherwise; the usage reference stays held and the function returns 0.
note: Checked reviewer claims against main.c:2113-2189: 'smart_suspend condition reversed' is wrong (line 2132 smart_suspend = !pm_runtime_block_if_disabled, line 2169-2170 matches prose); 'syscore path does not always block' is consistent with the qualified wording (block is whatever pm_runtime_block_if_disabled does at line 2132); syscore early return at 2134-2135 confirmed. Rewrote direct_complete as assigned true/false rather than only set true.

name: rpm_idle
prose: Precondition: the caller holds dev->power.lock with interrupts disabled; rpmflags may contain RPM_ASYNC and RPM_GET_PUT; the lock may be released and retaken around a synchronous runtime_idle callback and is held again on return. Postcondition: the function first evaluates rpm_check_suspend_allowed(dev). A negative result is returned as is (-EINVAL when runtime_error is set, -EACCES when disable_depth > 0, -EAGAIN when usage_count is nonzero or a resume is deferred or pending, -EBUSY when child_count is nonzero and ignore_children is clear, -EPERM when the PM QoS resume latency is 0). A result of 1 (device already RPM_SUSPENDED) is returned as 1 when RPM_GET_PUT is set, and otherwise falls to the next test and becomes -EAGAIN because runtime_status is not RPM_ACTIVE. For a zero result: -EAGAIN is returned if runtime_status is not RPM_ACTIVE or a pending request with a value above RPM_REQ_IDLE exists, and -EINPROGRESS if an idle notification is already in progress. If none of these apply, dev->power.request is set to RPM_REQ_NONE and then: with no runtime_idle callback or dev->power.no_callbacks set, the function returns rpm_suspend(dev, rpmflags | RPM_AUTO); with RPM_ASYNC set it sets request to RPM_REQ_IDLE, queues dev->power.work if no request was pending, and returns 0 without calling rpm_suspend; otherwise it sets idle_notification, releases the lock around the callback, retakes it, clears idle_notification, wakes dev->power.wait_queue, and returns the callback's value if nonzero, or rpm_suspend(dev, rpmflags | RPM_AUTO) if the callback returned 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (code converts 1 to -EAGAIN and ignores RPM_GET_PUT) is wrong: runtime.c:501-502 keeps retval == 1 when RPM_GET_PUT is set and line 520-521/562 returns it; only without RPM_GET_PUT does it become -EAGAIN (505-506). Earlier claims (async returns 0 directly, no_callbacks path calls rpm_suspend, other errnos from callback) are right. Added -EPERM from rpm_check_suspend_allowed (line 289-290).

name: rpm_suspend
prose: Precondition: the caller holds dev->power.lock with interrupts disabled; rpmflags may contain RPM_ASYNC, RPM_NOWAIT and RPM_AUTO; the lock is released and retaken at several points (the wait for another suspend, the runtime_suspend callback, the parent idle notification, suspending suppliers) and is held again on return. Postcondition: a nonzero result of rpm_check_suspend_allowed is returned unchanged with the status untouched: a negative errno (-EINVAL, -EACCES, -EAGAIN, -EBUSY or -EPERM), or 1 when the device is already RPM_SUSPENDED. Next, -EAGAIN is returned when runtime_status is RPM_RESUMING and RPM_ASYNC is not set. With RPM_AUTO set and runtime_status not RPM_SUSPENDING, if the autosuspend expiration is still in the future the pending request is cleared, the suspend timer is started unless one already expires at or before that time, timer_autosuspends is set, and 0 is returned. Otherwise pending requests and the timer are canceled; if runtime_status is RPM_SUSPENDING the function returns -EINPROGRESS when RPM_ASYNC or RPM_NOWAIT is set, and otherwise waits for the other suspend to finish (spinning with the lock briefly released when irq_safe) and restarts from the top. When dev->power.no_callbacks is set success is assumed. Otherwise with RPM_ASYNC set the request is set to RPM_REQ_AUTOSUSPEND (if RPM_AUTO) or RPM_REQ_SUSPEND, the work is queued if none was pending, and 0 is returned without running the callback. Otherwise the status becomes RPM_SUSPENDING and the runtime_suspend callback runs via rpm_callback. If it fails, the wake irq check is disabled, the status returns to RPM_ACTIVE, deferred_resume is cleared and waiters are woken; then if runtime_error is clear, RPM_AUTO is set and pm_runtime_autosuspend_expiration is nonzero the function restarts from the top and returns what that attempt returns, otherwise pending requests and the timer are canceled and the callback's error is returned. On success (or assumed success) the status becomes RPM_SUSPENDED, the timer is deactivated, the parent's child_count is decremented unless it is already zero, and waiters are woken; if deferred_resume was set it is cleared, rpm_resume(dev, 0) is called and -EAGAIN is returned; otherwise if irq_safe is set it returns 0, else it issues rpm_idle(parent, RPM_ASYNC) when the parent exists and does not ignore children, calls rpm_suspend_suppliers when links_count > 0, and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (omits return 1 for already-suspended) is right: rpm_check_suspend_allowed returns 1 (runtime.c:291-292) and rpm_suspend does goto out with retval 1 (596-605). Earlier claims about -EACCES/-EBUSY and early failures leaving status unchanged are right; -EPERM is also possible (289-290). Rewrote.

name: device_get_next_child_node
prose: Precondition: dev is a valid device and child is either NULL or a handle to one of the children of dev's firmware node. Postcondition: the function returns fwnode_get_next_child_node(dev_fwnode(dev), child) and is a thin wrapper. dev_fwnode(dev) is the OF node's fwnode handle when CONFIG_OF is enabled and dev->of_node is set, and dev->fwnode otherwise. fwnode_get_next_child_node uses dev's firmware node as parent when child is NULL, otherwise child's parent (obtained with fwnode_get_parent and released automatically before it returns); it returns NULL if that parent is NULL or an error pointer; otherwise it returns the next child reported by the node's get_next_child_node operation, or, when the primary node has no further child, the first child of the parent's secondary firmware node, or NULL. A non-NULL result carries a reference the caller must release with fwnode_handle_put(). The function's documentation states that the reference to child is put unconditionally, so the caller's reference to child is consumed (the visible code does not call fwnode_handle_put on child itself; that is left to the underlying operation, and no put happens on the NULL return caused by a NULL or error-pointer parent).
note: Reviewer claims (round 2 and 15) are right: the doc comment at property.c:857-863 says 'this function also puts a reference to @child unconditionally'. The previous prose said the caller's child reference is not consumed, which was wrong.

name: regcache_sync_block_single
prose: Precondition: block points to cached values and cache_present to the presence bitmap, both indexed by i for i in [start, end); the register address for index i is block_base + i * map->reg_stride. Postcondition: the function scans i from start up to end-1 in order. For each index whose presence bit is set and whose register passes regmap_writeable, it reads the cached value with regcache_get_val and calls regcache_sync_val; regcache_sync_val itself skips the write and returns 0 when regcache_reg_needs_sync reports no sync is needed, and otherwise writes the value with the cache bypassed. If regcache_sync_val returns nonzero the function returns that error immediately without processing later indices; otherwise it returns 0 after the loop. Indices that are not present or whose register is not writeable are skipped.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (the shown code never checks regcache_reg_needs_sync) is wrong: regcache.c:750-755 regcache_sync_val returns 0 early when !regcache_reg_needs_sync, so the skip happens inside the callee called at line 790. Round 1 precondition-range complaint is also not an issue: loop is i = start; i < end (line 782).

name: regmap_mmio_regbits_check
prose: Precondition: reg_bits is the requested register width in bits (a size_t). Postcondition: the function returns 0 when reg_bits is 8, 16 or 32, and returns -EINVAL for any other value of reg_bits; it reads and writes no other state.
note: Mechanical reviewer complaint (formal contract omits EINVAL) is wrong: the contract's else branch is result == -22, which is -EINVAL (regmap-mmio.c:33-40). Prose matches the switch.

name: regmap_mmio_get_min_stride
prose: Precondition: val_bits is the requested value width in bits (a size_t). Postcondition: the function returns 0 when val_bits is 8 (the regmap core treats 0 as 1), 2 when val_bits is 16, 4 when val_bits is 32, and -EINVAL for any other value of val_bits; it reads and writes no other state.
note: Mechanical reviewer complaint (contract omits EINVAL) is wrong: final else branch is result == -22 (regmap-mmio.c:47-62).

name: __regmap_init
prose: Precondition: dev, bus and bus_context may be NULL as the callers allow; config may be NULL; lock_key and lock_name are used for lockdep on the default mutex or spinlock. Postcondition on success: it returns a newly allocated regmap in which the lock (no-op lock, config-supplied lock and unlock, hwspinlock, raw spinlock, spinlock or mutex), allocation flags, register and value format parameters, read and write callbacks, flag masks, async list and waitqueue, range tree built from config->ranges, and register cache (regcache_init) are set up, and either regmap_attach_dev(dev, map, config) is called when dev is non-NULL or regmap_debugfs_init(map) when dev is NULL. For configs with neither a bus read/write pair nor config read/write, or a bus without read and write, the format-handler and work-buffer step is skipped; otherwise the format_reg, format_val, format_write and parse handlers are selected from reg_bits plus pad shift, val_bits and the register and value endianness and a work buffer of format.buf_size bytes is allocated. On failure it returns ERR_PTR: -EINVAL for a NULL config, an unsupported reg_bits/val_bits/endianness combination, a format_write combination that is not big-endian for both register and value, missing format_reg/format_val handlers, or an invalid range definition (range_max below range_min, range_max or selector_reg above max_register, window_len 0, or a selector or window of another range inside this range); -ENOMEM when allocating the map, the work buffer, a range node or the selector work buffer fails; -ENXIO when hwspin_lock_request_specific fails; or the negative error of regmap_set_name, regcache_init or regmap_attach_dev. The failure paths free what was built so far (regcache, ranges, work buffer, hwspinlock, name, map as applicable) and, for every failure including a NULL config, free the bus with kfree when bus is non-NULL and bus->free_on_exit is set.
note: Slice cut the head (function starts at regmap.c:677); fixed under the real name. Enumerated the actual error paths: err (config NULL -> -EINVAL), err_map (regmap_set_name fails), err_name (-ENXIO hwlock), err_hwlock (-EINVAL unsupported formats, -ENOMEM work_buf), err_range, err_regcache. The bus is freed at the common err label (regmap.c:1177-1179).

name: amiga_floppy_init
prose: Precondition: none; this is the module initialization function. Postcondition: it returns the value of platform_driver_probe(&amiga_floppy_driver, amiga_floppy_probe) and has no other effect itself. That call returns -EINVAL when the driver is marked PROBE_PREFER_ASYNCHRONOUS, returns the error of __platform_driver_register when registration fails, returns -ENODEV (after unregistering the driver) when registration succeeded but no platform device ended up bound to the driver, which includes the case where amiga_floppy_probe returned an error for the device, and returns 0 when at least one platform device is bound. The errors of amiga_floppy_probe (-EBUSY, -ENOMEM, -ENODEV) are not returned to the caller of this function.
note: Slice cut the head. amiflop.c:1942-1945: body is a single return of platform_driver_probe; platform.c:912-957 shows the -EINVAL, register-error and -ENODEV paths. Reviewer round 15 claim (the code calls platform_driver_probe not platform_driver_register, and probe failures return -EBUSY/-ENOMEM too) is half right: it calls platform_driver_probe, but a failing probe leaves the device unbound so the result is -ENODEV, not the probe's own errno. Earlier prose naming platform_driver_register was wrong.

name: fd_rwsec_done1
prose: Precondition: called from the FDC completion or timeout path with the FDC status byte in status for the sector transfer in progress. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It first calls stop_timeout(); if SUDT->stretch is nonzero it reads the FDC track register and writes it back shifted left by SUDT->stretch. If UseTrackbuffer is false it writes 0x90 to dma_mode_status and, if bit 0 of the readback is clear, prints a DMA error and goes to the error path. It goes to the error path if ReqCmd is WRITE and status has FDCSTAT_WPROT. If status has FDCSTAT_RECNF and it is not the benign case (read_track set and the FDC sector register above SUDT->spt): when Probing is set, if SUDT is above atari_disk_type and SUDT[-1].blocks > ReqBlock then SUDT is decremented and set_capacity is updated, otherwise Probing is cleared (with an info message when SUDT is at atari_disk_type and SUD.flags has FTD_MSG); when Probing is clear and SUD.autoprobe is set, SUDT is reset to atari_disk_type + StartDiskType[DriveType], set_capacity is updated and Probing is set. If Probing is then set, fdc_speed is written when ATARIHW_PRESENT(FDCSPEED), setup_req_params and do_fd_action are called with BufferDrive set to -1, and the function returns without calling fd_error; otherwise it prints a 'sector not found' message and goes to the error path. It also goes to the error path if status has FDCSTAT_CRC or FDCSTAT_LOST. On the success path Probing is cleared; for a READ request, a non-track read flushes the cache for 512 bytes at ReqData when ATARIHW_PRESENT(EXTD_DMA) (no copy), otherwise for DMABuffer and then copies it to ReqData with copy_buffer, while a track read flushes the track buffer, records BufferDrive, BufferSide and BufferTrack and copies the requested sector to ReqData; then if ++ReqCnt is below blk_rq_cur_sectors(fd_request) it calls setup_req_params and do_fd_action for the next sector, otherwise it ends the current request with BLK_STS_OK and calls finish_fdc. The error path sets BufferDrive to -1 and calls fd_error.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim is right: ataflop.c:1236-1239 uses ReqData directly under EXTD_DMA and copy_buffer only when EXTD_DMA is absent; prose corrected. Original claim (RECNF while probing restarts via do_fd_action and returns without fd_error) is already stated and right (1205-1214). Also fixed the SUDT == atari_disk_type branch which clears Probing (1190-1195).

name: drbd_adm_attach
prose: Precondition: called as a generic netlink handler with skb and info. Postcondition: it calls drbd_adm_prepare(DRBD_ADM_NEED_MINOR); if adm_ctx.reply_skb is NULL it returns the retcode from prepare, and otherwise it returns 0 after calling drbd_adm_finish with the final retcode, so the outcome is reported in the reply code. If prepare reported an error it goes straight to drbd_adm_finish without taking adm_mutex; otherwise adm_mutex of the resource is held from after prepare until just before drbd_adm_finish. Reply codes set by this function on failure are ERR_DISK_CONFIGURED (disk state above D_DISKLESS), ERR_NOMEM, ERR_MANDATORY_TAG, ERR_MD_IDX_INVALID, ERR_STONITH_AND_PROT_A, the code returned by open_backing_devices (including ERR_OPEN_DISK and ERR_OPEN_MD_DISK), the code returned by drbd_md_read, ERR_DISK_TOO_SMALL, ERR_MD_DISK_TOO_SMALL, the state-change value returned for the D_ATTACHING request when it is below SS_SUCCESS, ERR_DATA_NOT_CURRENT, ERR_IMPLICIT_SHRINK, the code from drbd_resync_after_valid, ERR_NOMEM_BITMAP and ERR_IO_MD_DISK. If the final _drbd_set_state fails (rv below SS_SUCCESS), or get_ldev_if_state fails, the function leaves its attach and goes to the diskless cleanup without storing rv in retcode, so retcode keeps the value it held at that point. Failure before the point of no return frees nbc (closing the backing and meta device files), new_disk_conf, the resync LRU and the plan; failures after the D_ATTACHING request succeeded go through the diskless cleanup, which puts the ldev reference (unless get_ldev_if_state itself failed), calls drbd_force_state(D_DISKLESS) and drbd_md_sync. After the point of no return (where device->ldev, device->resync and device->rs_plan_s take over those allocations and the local pointers are set to NULL) the later failure paths do not free them. On success the new disk state is D_INCONSISTENT when MDF_CONSISTENT is not set, D_OUTDATED when it is set but MDF_WAS_UP_TO_DATE is not, otherwise D_CONSISTENT, which becomes D_UP_TO_DATE when the peer disk is D_OUTDATED or the fencing policy is FP_DONT_CARE; when device->state.conn is C_CONNECTED the decision is deferred and the disk state is set to D_NEGOTIATING. On success it also marks the metadata dirty and syncs it, sends a KOBJ_CHANGE uevent, puts the ldev reference and calls conn_reconfig_done.
note: Slice cut the head (function starts at drbd_nl.c:1735). Reviewer round 15 claim is right: open_backing_devices can return ERR_OPEN_DISK/ERR_OPEN_MD_DISK (assigned to retcode at line 1835). Previous prose said 'always returns 0' and omitted the reply_skb NULL early return correctly but overstated; also the _drbd_set_state failure at line 2117 does not update retcode.

name: conn_try_disconnect
prose: Precondition: connection is a valid drbd_connection and the caller serializes network reconfiguration (drbd_adm_disconnect holds adm_mutex). Postcondition: it requests C_DISCONNECTING with conn_request_state (flag CS_HARD when force is true) and examines the result rv. SS_ALREADY_STANDALONE makes it return SS_SUCCESS at once, without stopping the receiver or issuing the final C_STANDALONE request; this also applies after a retry through the repeat label. SS_NOTHING_TO_DO is kept as rv. SS_PRIMARY_NOP triggers a second request with pdsk set to D_OUTDATED and, if that returns SS_OUTDATE_WO_CONN, a third plain C_DISCONNECTING request with CS_VERBOSE; rv becomes the last of these results. SS_CW_FAILED_BY_PEER reads the connection state under req_lock: when it is C_WF_CONNECTION or lower the whole request is repeated from the start; otherwise it requests C_DISCONNECTING with disk D_OUTDATED and, if that returns SS_IS_DISKLESS or SS_LOWER_THAN_OUTDATED, requests C_DISCONNECTING again with CS_HARD; rv becomes the last result. Any other result is kept as rv. If rv is at least SS_SUCCESS (which includes SS_NOTHING_TO_DO, whose value is 2) it stops the receiver thread with drbd_thread_stop and issues a final C_STANDALONE request with CS_VERBOSE | CS_HARD whose result is only logged when below SS_SUCCESS. The function returns rv (the last disconnect-request result, not the final C_STANDALONE result), except for the early SS_SUCCESS return; when rv is below SS_SUCCESS, the receiver is not stopped and no C_STANDALONE request is made.
note: Reviewer rounds all partly right: original (returns rv not rv2; early ALREADY_STANDALONE skips receiver stop) right; round 2 (SS_NOTHING_TO_DO and SS_PRIMARY_NOP are >= SS_SUCCESS) right for SS_NOTHING_TO_DO=2 (drbd.h:284); SS_PRIMARY_NOP=-7 is below SS_SUCCESS so only its retry result matters; round 15 right only for the goto repeat case (drbd_nl.c:2686-2691); an ALREADY_STANDALONE result from the retry requests at lines 2680/2693 is returned as rv. Rewrote.

name: drbd_seq_show
prose: Precondition: seq is a valid seq_file; v is not used by this function. Postcondition: the function writes the version and build tag header lines, then holds the RCU read lock while it walks every entry of drbd_devices with idr_for_each_entry. For each device it writes a newline first when the index is not consecutive with the previous one, then either a '%2d: cs:Unconfigured' line when the device state is C_STANDALONE, D_DISKLESS and R_SECONDARY, or the state line (connection state, roles, disk states, wire protocol letter, flag letters, counters and write ordering letter) followed by the ' oos:' line. When the connection state is C_SYNC_SOURCE, C_SYNC_TARGET, C_VERIFY_S or C_VERIFY_T it calls drbd_syncer_progress. When drbd_proc_details is at least 1 and get_ldev_if_state(device, D_FAILED) succeeds it prints resync and activity-log LRU statistics and puts the ldev reference. When drbd_proc_details is at least 2 it prints the 'blocked on activity log' line. It releases the RCU read lock and returns 0; it is the only return in the function.
note: Slice cut the head. Round 15 reviewer claim (v used for SEQ_START_TOKEN, header not written on every call, early return omitted) is wrong for this source: drbd_proc.c:215-323 never reads v, has a single return 0 at the end, and writes the header unconditionally at 230-231. Previous prose precondition about no RCU lock/ldev removed (not required by the code).

name: drbd_asb_recover_1p
prose: Precondition: the caller holds a local disk reference (the function is annotated __must_hold(local)) and peer_device->connection->net_conf is non-NULL under RCU; the function takes and releases the RCU read lock only around reading after_sb_1p. Postcondition: it returns one of -100, -1 or 1 (the verdict hg of drbd_asb_recover_0p can only be -100, -1 or 1), chosen by after_sb_1p: for ASB_DISCARD_YOUNGER_PRI, ASB_DISCARD_OLDER_PRI, ASB_DISCARD_LEAST_CHG, ASB_DISCARD_LOCAL, ASB_DISCARD_REMOTE and ASB_DISCARD_ZERO_CHG it logs a configuration error and returns -100; for ASB_DISCONNECT it returns -100; for ASB_CONSENSUS it calls drbd_asb_recover_0p and returns -1 if the verdict is -1 and the local role is R_SECONDARY, 1 if the verdict is 1 and the local role is R_PRIMARY, and -100 otherwise; for ASB_VIOLENTLY it returns the verdict of drbd_asb_recover_0p unchanged (-100, -1 or 1); for ASB_DISCARD_SECONDARY it returns 1 when the local role is R_PRIMARY and -1 otherwise; for ASB_CALL_HELPER it calls drbd_asb_recover_0p and, when the verdict is -1 and the local role is R_PRIMARY, tries drbd_change_state to R_SECONDARY: on SS_SUCCESS it returns -1, otherwise it runs the pri-lost-after-sb helper and returns -100; in all other ASB_CALL_HELPER cases it returns the verdict unchanged (-100, -1 or 1, including -1 with local secondary and 1 with either role); for an after_sb_1p value not listed it returns -100.
note: Slice cut the head (function starts at drbd_receiver.c:2917). Reviewer round 2 (CALL_HELPER with 1 and local secondary returns 1; ASB_VIOLENTLY omitted) right; round 15 claim that CALL_HELPER with -1 and local secondary should be -1 is right (line 2964-2965 rv = hg). Previous prose wrongly listed that case under 1 and used 'never 0' wording.

name: after_state_ch
prose: Precondition: device is a valid drbd_device, os and ns are the old and new device states of a completed state change, flags are the change flags and state_change is the snapshot to broadcast; the function may sleep and runs in the after-state-change work. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It calls broadcast_state_change(state_change), fills a sib_info and calls drbd_bcast_event, clears CRASHED_PRIMARY and the peer UUID flag bit when both disks became D_UP_TO_DATE, and runs pri-on-incon-degr when the local node became primary with both disks below D_UP_TO_DATE. Depending on the transition between os and ns it then may: restart or resend frozen requests when susp_nod or susp_fen is set; send the sync UUID when it became sync source with protocol 96 or newer; reset resync counters and send UUIDs and state when the peer disk attached; queue a bitmap send when entering C_WF_BITMAP_S; create a new current UUID and send UUIDs after contact to the peer's data was lost or the peer became primary with an empty bitmap; write the bitmap on demote or when a diskless peer became secondary; send sizes, UUIDs and state at the end of attaching; send the state on resync-pause flag changes, on leaving C_WF_REPORT_PARAMS, on entering C_AHEAD, when a resync target finished, when a verify finished, and when the disk dropped from D_UP_TO_DATE to D_INCONSISTENT while connected; suspend or resume other sync groups (suspend_other_sg, resume_next_sg); queue a set-and-write bitmap I/O when starting a full sync; handle the first half of a local disk failure (local-io-error helper, aborting disk I/O after a forced detach, sending state, cancelling resync, drbd_md_sync, put_ldev) and the second half of going diskless (send state, put_ldev); run resync_after_online_grow after a grow while detached; and queue a bitmap write after a resync ended. It finishes with drbd_md_sync(device). Each of these steps is conditional on the matching os/ns comparison and none is guaranteed to run for a given call.
note: Slice cut the head: the packet text is the middle of after_state_ch (drbd_state.c:1708-2035), not a function named after_state_chg taking a drbd_work (that is w_after_state_ch at 1489, which only calls after_state_ch). Fixed under the real name; prose is a summary of all the conditional blocks, each checked against 1717-2034.

name: is_valid_conn_transition
prose: Precondition: oc and nc are values of enum drbd_conns; the function reads no other state. Postcondition: the checks are applied in this order and the first one that matches decides the result: SS_NOTHING_TO_DO when oc equals nc; SS_ALREADY_STANDALONE when oc is C_STANDALONE and nc is C_DISCONNECTING; SS_NEED_CONNECTION when oc is C_STANDALONE and nc is not C_UNCONNECTED; SS_NEED_CONNECTION when oc is below C_WF_REPORT_PARAMS and nc is at least C_CONNECTED; SS_IN_TRANSIENT_STATE when oc is between C_TIMEOUT and C_TEAR_DOWN inclusive and nc is neither C_UNCONNECTED nor C_DISCONNECTING; SS_IN_TRANSIENT_STATE when oc is C_DISCONNECTING and nc is not C_STANDALONE; and SS_SUCCESS when none of those matched.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures result == ((oc == nc) ? SS_NOTHING_TO_DO : ((oc == C_STANDALONE && nc == C_DISCONNECTING) ? SS_ALREADY_STANDALONE : ((oc == C_STANDALONE && nc != C_UNCONNECTED) ? SS_NEED_CONNECTION : ((oc < C_WF_REPORT_PARAMS && nc >= C_CONNECTED) ? SS_NEED_CONNECTION : ((oc >= C_TIMEOUT && oc <= C_TEAR_DOWN && nc != C_UNCONNECTED && nc != C_DISCONNECTING) ? SS_IN_TRANSIENT_STATE : ((oc == C_DISCONNECTING && nc != C_STANDALONE) ? SS_IN_TRANSIENT_STATE : SS_SUCCESS)))))); */
note: Reviewer round 2 right (oc == nc == C_STANDALONE returns SS_NOTHING_TO_DO first, drbd_state.c:977-978) and round 15 right (C_DISCONNECTING transient applies for any nc != C_STANDALONE, line 998-999, not just nc < C_CONNECTED). Contract rewritten as a first-match chain mirroring lines 977-1001.

name: do_floppy_init
prose: Precondition: called once from module initialization (directly for a module build, or from the async init for a built-in). Postcondition: on CONFIG_PPC builds it first returns -ENODEV if check_legacy_ioport(FDC1) fails, before allocating anything. It then allocates the ordered workqueue floppy_wq (returning -ENOMEM at once if that fails) and, for each of N_DRIVE drives, a blk-mq tag set and a gendisk via floppy_alloc_disk; an error from either goes to out_put_disk. It then registers the block major with floppy_probe (__register_blkdev), registers the floppy platform driver, fills floppy_sizes, resets fdc_state, and if fdc_state[0].address is -1 cancels fd_timeout and fails with -ENODEV. floppy_grab_irq_and_dma failure cancels fd_timeout and fails with -EBUSY. It then initializes drive_state, probes each FDC with user_reset_fdc and get_fdc_version (releasing the regions of a controller that fails and clearing have_no_fdc, which starts at -ENODEV, for each usable controller), cancels fd_timeout, sets current_drive to 0 and sets initialized to true before the have_no_fdc test. If have_no_fdc is still set it fails with that value (-ENODEV). Otherwise, for each available drive it registers a platform device and calls device_add_disk; an error from either fails with that errno. The function returns 0 only when all of that succeeded. The failure labels unwind in this order: out_remove_drives (del_gendisk and platform_device_unregister for the drives before the failing one that are available), out_release_dma (floppy_release_irq_and_dma if usage_count is nonzero), out_unreg_driver (platform_driver_unregister), out_unreg_blkdev (unregister_blkdev), out_put_disk (destroy_workqueue, then for each drive with an allocated disk timer_delete_sync, put_disk and blk_mq_free_tag_set); a jump to a label runs that label's step and all later ones. initialized stays true on the failure paths that come after the assignment, i.e. the have_no_fdc failure and the later registration failures.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (initialized is set at end, false on failures) is wrong: floppy.c:4710 sets initialized = true before the have_no_fdc test at 4711. Round 2 (PPC and workqueue returns are direct; PPC path does not cancel fd_timeout) is already covered and right. Prose condensed but keeps exact paths.

name: loop_set_status
prose: Precondition: lo is a loop device and info points to a valid loop_info64; the caller does not hold lo->lo_mutex. Postcondition: it returns the error of mutex_lock_killable at once if locking is interrupted, without freezing the queue. Once the lock is held it returns -ENXIO (after releasing lo_mutex, queue not frozen) when lo_state is not Lo_bound. Otherwise, if info->lo_offset or info->lo_sizelimit differs from the current values it sets size_changed and calls sync_blockdev and invalidate_bdev. It freezes the queue and calls loop_set_status_from_info; if that fails the queue is unfrozen, lo_mutex is released and its error is returned. On success it sets partscan when LO_FLAGS_PARTSCAN was not set in lo_flags but is set in info->lo_flags, updates lo_flags (clearing LOOP_SET_STATUS_CLEARABLE_FLAGS and setting the LOOP_SET_STATUS_SETTABLE_FLAGS bits of info->lo_flags), calls loop_update_dio, unfreezes the queue, clears GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN when partscan is set, recomputes and sets the device size with loop_set_size while still holding lo_mutex when size_changed, releases lo_mutex, calls loop_reread_partitions when partscan is set, and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (size update occurs before mutex_unlock, not after) is right: loop.c:1271-1276 loop_set_size is before mutex_unlock. Round 1 and 2 claims (early failure returns without lock/unfreeze; ENXIO path never freezes) right and already reflected.

name: loop_change_fd
prose: Precondition: arg is a file descriptor number, lo is a loop device with a valid lo_disk, and bdev is lo's block device. Postcondition: if fget(arg) fails it returns -EBADF; if loop_check_backing_file rejects the file (no read_iter, or writable without write_iter) it puts the new file reference and returns -EINVAL; in both cases uevent suppression is untouched and no uevent is emitted. Otherwise it sets uevent suppression on the disk, takes the global lock with loop_global_lock_killable (is_loop depends on whether file is a loop device) and, if that fails, puts the new file reference, clears uevent suppression, emits KOBJ_CHANGE and returns that lock error. Under the lock, it fails (releasing the lock, putting the new file, clearing suppression, emitting KOBJ_CHANGE) with -ENXIO when lo_state is not Lo_bound, -EINVAL when LO_FLAGS_READ_ONLY is not set, the error returned by loop_validate_file(file, bdev) when that fails, or -EINVAL when lo_calculate_size for the new file differs from that of the old backing file; lo->lo_backing_file is unchanged on these failures. On success it calls vfs_fsync on the new file (result ignored), disk_force_media_change, freezes the queue, restores the old file's mapping gfp mask, installs the new file with loop_assign_backing_file (which sets the new file's gfp mask, may set LO_FLAGS_DIRECT_IO and sets lo_min_dio_size), calls loop_update_dio, unfreezes the queue, reads LO_FLAGS_PARTSCAN, releases the lock, briefly takes and releases loop_validate_mutex when the file is not a loop device, drops the old file reference with fput, clears uevent suppression, rereads partitions if LO_FLAGS_PARTSCAN was set, emits KOBJ_CHANGE and returns 0; the lo device keeps the reference to the new file.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (loop_validate_file error is propagated, not forced to -EINVAL) is right: loop.c:575-577 error = loop_validate_file(); goto out_err. Round 2 claim (early fget/check failures return without restoring suppression or uevent) right: prose already said so; round 1 (lock error such as -ERESTARTSYS) is covered by 'that lock error'.

name: rnbd_to_bio_flags
prose: Precondition: rnbd_opf is any u32 whose low 8 bits (RNBD_OP_MASK) hold an RNBD opcode and whose higher bits may hold RNBD_F_SYNC (bit 8) and RNBD_F_FUA (bit 9). Postcondition: the function returns a blk_opf_t built as follows: RNBD_OP_READ gives REQ_OP_READ, RNBD_OP_WRITE gives REQ_OP_WRITE, RNBD_OP_FLUSH gives REQ_OP_WRITE | REQ_PREFLUSH, RNBD_OP_DISCARD gives REQ_OP_DISCARD, RNBD_OP_SECURE_ERASE gives REQ_OP_SECURE_ERASE, RNBD_OP_WRITE_ZEROES gives REQ_OP_WRITE_ZEROES, and any other opcode triggers a WARN and gives 0; REQ_SYNC is then ORed in if RNBD_F_SYNC is set in rnbd_opf and REQ_FUA is ORed in if RNBD_F_FUA is set. It reads and writes no other state.
note: Slice cut the head (function at rnbd-proto.h:219-255). Previous prose and contract used wrong numeric REQ_* values (reviewers rounds 1,2,15 right: REQ_SYNC, REQ_FUA, REQ_PREFLUSH are bit flags at __REQ_* positions in blk_types.h, not 8/512/1025). Contract left empty because REQ_* values come from kernel headers.

name: xen_blkif_get
note: Not a function: object-like macro at common.h:365 `#define xen_blkif_get(_b) (atomic_inc(&(_b)->refcnt))` that only forwards to atomic_inc.

name: xen_blkif_put
note: Not a function: macro at common.h:366-370 expanding to do { if (atomic_dec_and_test(&(_b)->refcnt)) schedule_work(&(_b)->free_work); } while (0).

name: btusb_probe
prose: Precondition: intf is a USB interface matched to this driver and id is its usb_device_id (replaced by the usb_match_id match in quirks_table when id->driver_info is 0 and a match exists). Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV, before allocating anything, when id->driver_info has BTUSB_IFNUM_2 and the interface number is neither 0 nor 2, when driver_info is BTUSB_IGNORE, or when it has BTUSB_ATH3012 with bcdDevice at most 0x0001 and btusb_qca_need_patch is false. It returns -ENOMEM when allocating btusb_data fails, and -ENODEV (after freeing btusb_data) when usb_find_common_endpoints finds no bulk-in, bulk-out and interrupt endpoints. It then allocates the hci_dev (-ENOMEM after freeing btusb_data on failure) and configures data and hdev from the driver_info flags. Later failures: gpiod_get_optional or btusb_config_oob_wake failing returns that error after putting the reset GPIO if one was obtained, freeing hdev and freeing data; marvell_config_oob_wake failing also disables device wakeup when an OOB wake irq exists before the same frees; btintel_configure_setup failing, usb_set_interface failing for BTUSB_INTEL_BOOT, or usb_driver_claim_interface failing for the isoc interface additionally kills the anchored TX URBs first (the isoc interface that failed to claim is not released); hci_register_dev failing additionally releases the claimed diag and isoc interfaces (clearing their interface data) before the URB kill. On those paths the function returns the errno from the failing call. It returns 0 after hci_register_dev succeeds, usb_set_intfdata(intf, data) is done and the force_poll_sync debugfs file is created. A failure to claim the diag interface is not an error; it only clears data->diag.
note: Slice cut the head (function starts at btusb.c:4048). Reviewer round 15 right: the early failures (gpiod, OOB wake) do not kill TX URBs or release claimed interfaces (labels out_free_dev / err_disable_wakeup / err_kill_tx_urbs / err_release_siblings at 4427-4446 are a cascade). Rewrote with per-label effects.

name: intel_set_power
prose: Precondition: hu is a valid hci_uart and hu->tty is non-NULL (hu->tty->dev is dereferenced). Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV at once if hu->tty->dev is NULL. Otherwise it takes intel_device_list_lock and walks intel_device_list, skipping entries whose pdev parent differs from hu->tty->dev->parent; the lock is released before the function returns. The return value starts as -ENODEV. For a matching entry with no reset GPIO it sets the value to -ENOTSUPP and stops the walk without touching idev->hu. For a matching entry with a reset GPIO it calls gpiod_set_value(idev->reset, powered), sets idev->hu to hu when powered is true and to NULL when false under idev->hu_lock, and then stops the walk if idev->irq is negative (return value unchanged, so -ENODEV unless set earlier). With idev->irq non-negative, if powered is true and the pdev can wake up it requests the threaded irq: on failure the value becomes that error and the walk stops; on success the value becomes 0, wakeup is enabled, runtime PM is set active, autosuspend is enabled with LPM_SUSPEND_DELAY_MS and runtime PM is enabled, and the walk continues with the next list entry. If powered is false and the pdev may wake up it frees the irq, disables wakeup, disables autosuspend and runtime PM, leaving the return value unchanged; if powered is true and the pdev cannot wake up it does nothing more and leaves the value unchanged. So for a single matching device the result is -ENOTSUPP without a reset GPIO, -ENODEV with a negative irq, or when powering off, or when powering on a device that cannot wake up, the irq request error on failure, and 0 on a successful power-on.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (power-off path can return -ENOTSUPP when the matching device lacks reset) is right (hci_intel.c:306-309 precedes any powered test). Round 2 (-ENODEV when powered on but device_can_wakeup false) and original (idev->hu not set when reset is NULL; -ENOTSUPP) are right. The walk does not break on a successful power-on (no break after line 346), so the value can be overwritten by later matching entries; qualified as 'for a single matching device'.

name: qca_controller_memdump
prose: Precondition: the ctrl_memdump_evt work item runs for a qca_data whose hu is valid; frames of the controller memory dump are queued on qca->rx_memdump_q. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It loops on skb_dequeue(&qca->rx_memdump_q), taking qca->hci_memdump_lock (a mutex) only after each skb has been dequeued, and the lock is released before every return and at the end of every iteration. It returns immediately, leaving the dequeued skb neither appended nor freed and later frames still queued, when memdump_state is QCA_MEMDUMP_TIMEOUT or QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTED, or when allocating a missing qca_memdump fails. Otherwise it sets memdump_state to QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTING and pulls the header. For sequence number 0 it sets QCA_IBS_DISABLED and QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTION and reads ram_dump_size; if that size is 0 it frees qca_memdump (qca->qca_memdump becomes NULL), sets the state to QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTED, clears and wakes QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTION, clears QCA_IBS_DISABLED, frees the skb and returns; otherwise it queues ctrl_memdump_timeout, resets current_seq_no and received_dump and calls hci_devcd_init, and if that fails it frees qca->qca_memdump (set to NULL), sets the state to QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTED, cancels the timeout, clears QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTION and QCA_IBS_DISABLED, and returns without freeing the skb. If QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTION is clear it frees the local qca_memdump pointer (qca->qca_memdump is left pointing at freed memory when it was the same object), frees the skb and returns. Otherwise it fills gaps for missed packets with hci_devcd_append_pattern (skipped for QCA_QCA6390 and for the last sequence number, stopping when the space is exhausted), then appends the skb with hci_devcd_append and advances current_seq_no and received_dump when received_dump plus skb->len fits in ram_dump_size; when it does not fit, the skb is neither appended nor freed. For QCA_LAST_SEQUENCE_NUM it calls hci_devcd_complete, cancels the timeout, frees qca->qca_memdump (set to NULL) and sets the state to QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTED and clears QCA_MEMDUMP_COLLECTION without clearing QCA_IBS_DISABLED.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim is right: skb_dequeue at hci_qca.c:1046 precedes mutex_lock at 1048. Round 2 (no-space and devcd_init-failure paths leave the skb neither appended nor freed) right (1160-1177, 1106-1114); original (omits early returns) addressed.

name: mhi_init_mmio
prose: Precondition: mhi_cntrl is an initialized controller whose regs, reg_len, mhi_ctxt, channel and event arrays and iova range are set. Postcondition: it reads the channel doorbell offset with mhi_get_channel_doorbell_offset and returns its error if that fails; it returns -ERANGE if that offset is at least reg_len - 8 * MHI_DEV_WAKE_DB. Then it sets wake_db and wake_set = false and every channel's tre_ring.db_addr from the offset. It reads ERDBOFF (returning -EIO if the read fails) and returns -ERANGE if the offset is at least reg_len - 8 * total_ev_rings (the earlier wake and channel doorbell assignments remain done); it then sets the doorbell address of every event ring that is not offload_ev and the primary command ring's db_addr to base + CRDB_LOWER, writes the table of context, control-base, data-base and limit registers (stopping at the zero-offset sentinel), and writes the MHICFG NER and NHWER fields, returning the error from the first of those two writes that fails. It returns 0 after all of that succeeds.
note: Slice cut the head; function is mhi_init_mmio at init.c:469-607, so fixed rather than dropped. Prose checked against 540-606.

name: mhi_process_data_event_ring
prose: Precondition: mhi_cntrl and mhi_event describe a data event ring with valid event context and ring storage; event_quota is the number of TX or RSC events that may be processed. Postcondition: it returns -EIO, consuming nothing, if MHI_EVENT_ACCESS_INVALID(pm_state) is true or the context read pointer is outside the event ring. Otherwise, while the device read pointer differs from the local read pointer and event_quota is above zero, it reads the event's type and channel; if the channel is below max_chan and configured, it handles an MHI_PKT_TYPE_TX_EVENT with parse_xfer_event or an MHI_PKT_TYPE_RSC_TX_EVENT with parse_rsc_event and decrements event_quota for each; events of other types, or for unconfigured or out-of-range channels, are not handled and do not decrement event_quota. Each element is recycled with mhi_recycle_ev_ring_element and the device read pointer is re-read; if the re-read pointer is outside the ring it returns -EIO at that point (some elements already recycled, doorbell not rung); otherwise count is incremented. After the loop it takes pm_lock for reading and rings the event doorbell with mhi_ring_er_db only if MHI_DB_ACCESS_VALID(mhi_cntrl) and count is nonzero, releases the lock, and returns count, the number of recycled elements (possibly 0).
note: Slice cut the head; function is mhi_process_data_event_ring (main.c:995-1067). Previous prose mostly right; added that non-TX/RSC events and unconfigured channels are recycled without handling and without using quota.

name: mhi_pm_suspend
prose: Precondition: mhi_cntrl points to an initialized MHI controller whose pm_lock, state_event, lpm_chans list, wake_get/wake_put callbacks and timeout_ms are usable. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if pm_state is MHI_PM_DISABLE, -EIO if pm_state is already an error state, and -EBUSY if dev_wake or pending_pkts is nonzero, all before this function changes anything. Otherwise it takes a wake reference (wake_get under pm_lock) and waits up to timeout_ms for dev_state M0 or M1 or an error pm_state, then releases the wake reference with wake_put; if the wait timed out or pm_state is an error state it returns -EIO (this function has not changed pm_state). It then takes pm_lock for writing and returns -EBUSY (pm_state not changed by this function) if dev_wake or pending_pkts became nonzero; calls mhi_tryset_pm_state(MHI_PM_M3_ENTER) and returns -EIO if the resulting state is not MHI_PM_M3_ENTER; otherwise pm_state is now MHI_PM_M3_ENTER, it calls mhi_set_mhi_state(MHI_STATE_M3), releases the lock and waits up to timeout_ms for dev_state M3 or an error pm_state. If that wait times out or pm_state is an error state it returns -EIO and leaves pm_state as it is (MHI_PM_M3_ENTER or whatever another context set it to). On success it notifies each device on lpm_chans that has an mhi_dev with MHI_CB_LPM_ENTER under that channel's mutex and returns 0.
note: Reviewer claims all right: original (timeout after setting M3_ENTER leaves pm_state changed), round 2 (omits -EIO when mhi_tryset_pm_state fails, pm.c:915-923) and round 15 (pm_state may have changed to an error state when the wait sees an error state) are right; prose now says 'this function has not changed pm_state' for the early paths rather than 'unchanged'.

name: mvebu_mbus_dt_init
prose: Precondition: is_coherent says whether the platform has hardware I/O coherency; the function finds its own device-tree node and takes no node argument. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV (printing an error) when no node matches of_mvebu_mbus_ids; it records the matching SoC data in mbus_state.soc; it returns -EINVAL when the node has no 'controller' property, -ENODEV when that phandle does not resolve to a node, and -EINVAL when register resource 0 (MBUS) or resource 1 (SDRAM) of the controller node cannot be read. It then zeroes mbusbridge_res, tries resource 2 only when the SoC has an mbus bridge and only prints a firmware warning when it is missing, stores is_coherent in mbus_state.hw_io_coherency, reads the optional pcie-mem-aperture and pcie-io-aperture properties into mbus_state, and calls mvebu_mbus_common_init, returning its error if nonzero. Finally it returns the result of mbus_dt_setup for the statically declared windows (0 if the node has no parseable ranges, otherwise the first negative error from mbus_dt_setup_win, or 0 after all). The device-node references obtained by of_find_matching_node_and_match and of_find_node_by_phandle are not released by this function on any return path.
note: Slice cut the head; real function is mvebu_mbus_dt_init (mvebu-mbus.c:1249-1319), previously dropped. Earlier prose wrongly described a caller-provided node and an of_find_node_by_phandle reference being 'owned by the caller'; it takes no node argument.

name: intel_gtt_setup_scratch_page
prose: Precondition: intel_private.pcidev is set and, when intel_private.needs_dmar is set, usable for DMA mapping; the function takes no arguments. Postcondition: it allocates one zeroed GFP_DMA32 page; if the allocation fails it returns -ENOMEM and changes no state. Otherwise it marks the page uncacheable with set_pages_uc. When needs_dmar is set it maps the page with dma_map_page for bidirectional DMA; if the mapping fails it frees the page with __free_page (without reverting the uncacheable attribute) and returns -EINVAL with intel_private.scratch_page and scratch_page_dma not modified; on success it stores the DMA address in intel_private.scratch_page_dma. When needs_dmar is clear it stores page_to_phys(page) in scratch_page_dma. On those success paths it stores the page in intel_private.scratch_page and returns 0; the driver owns the page afterwards.
note: Function is intel_gtt_setup_scratch_page (intel-gtt.c:296-321), takes no arguments and touches global state, so contract left empty. Previous prose omitted that the page stays set uncacheable on the DMA-error path.

name: ac_ioctl
prose: Precondition: file is an open applicom device file, cmd is the ioctl command and arg points to user memory holding a struct st_ram_io (also writable for commands 0, 1 and 4). Postcondition: it copies the structure from user space with memdup_user and returns the negative errno of that copy at once if it fails, before taking any lock. Otherwise it takes ac_mutex and computes IndexCard = num_card - 1 (as an unsigned char); every return after this point frees the kernel copy and releases ac_mutex. If cmd is not 6 and IndexCard is MAX_BOARD or more, or the selected board's RamIO is NULL, it prints a warning (while the static warncount allows) and returns -EINVAL; this check runs before the command switch, so an unsupported cmd other than 6 can also give -EINVAL here. Otherwise the switch handles command 0 (read the board RAM into the structure and copy it to user space), 1 (read configuration fields and copy to user space), 2 (write the pattern and data_from_pc_ready and acknowledge, then read RAM_IT_TO_PC of all boards), 3 (write tic_des_from_pc), 4 (read owner fields and copy to user space), 5 (write num_card to the three card-number registers and set DATA_FROM_PC_READY and RAM_IT_FROM_PC) and 6 (print driver and board information); for commands 0, 1 and 4 a failed copy_to_user gives -EFAULT, for the other supported commands the result is 0, and any other command gives -ENOTTY. For cmd other than 6 it then reads the board's VERS register into Dummy.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: -EINVAL comes from the err label for an invalid IndexCard or missing RamIO (applicom.c:719-724, 846-854), not from adgl->num_card range as stated before; also command 0 is supported (prose said 1..6). Round 2 claim about -ENOTTY unaffected. Function is ac_ioctl at applicom.c:697.

name: hangcheck_fire
prose: Precondition: hangcheck_tsc holds the nanosecond timestamp saved by the previous firing or by init, hangcheck_tsc_margin the allowed gap in nanoseconds, and the module parameters hangcheck_tick, hangcheck_dump_tasks and hangcheck_reboot hold their configured values. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It reads ktime_get_ns() as cur_tsc and computes tsc_diff as cur_tsc - hangcheck_tsc when cur_tsc is greater than hangcheck_tsc, and as cur_tsc + (~0ULL - hangcheck_tsc) otherwise. If tsc_diff exceeds hangcheck_tsc_margin: when hangcheck_dump_tasks is nonzero it prints 'Hangcheck: Task state:' and, only when CONFIG_MAGIC_SYSRQ is defined, calls handle_sysrq('t'); then if hangcheck_reboot is nonzero it prints a restart message and calls emergency_restart(), which is not expected to return (in that case the timer is not rearmed and hangcheck_tsc is not updated), otherwise it prints 'Hangcheck: hangcheck value past margin!'. When the function does reach its end it rearms hangcheck_ticktock with mod_timer for hangcheck_tick * HZ jiffies from now and sets hangcheck_tsc to a fresh ktime_get_ns() reading.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (else branch computes cur_tsc - hangcheck_tsc - 1) is wrong as a source reading: hangcheck-timer.c:125 is cur_tsc + (~0ULL - hangcheck_tsc), which equals that value modulo 2^64 but is written differently; prose now states the exact expression. Round 2 (dump_tasks printing conditional) right; original (not rearmed on emergency_restart) right; hangcheck_tsc is refreshed from a second ktime_get_ns() call (line 149), not cur_tsc.

name: hpet_ioctl_ieon
prose: Precondition: devp is a valid hpet_dev with valid hd_timer, hd_hpet and hd_hpets pointers. Postcondition: it returns -EIO, with no flag change, if hd_ireqfreq is zero. Under hpet_lock it returns -EBUSY, with no flag change, if HPET_IE is already set in hd_flags; otherwise it sets HPET_IE and, if the timer config has Tn_INT_TYPE_CNF_MASK set, also HPET_SHARED_IRQ, then releases the lock. If hd_hdwirq is nonzero and the IRQ is shared, it clears Tn_TYPE_CNF_MASK in the timer config, writes the compare register from the main counter and clears the timer's bit in the ISR. If hd_hdwirq is nonzero it then names the device and calls request_irq; when that fails it logs an error and treats the IRQ as 0. If hd_hdwirq is zero or request_irq failed, it toggles HPET_IE back off under hpet_lock (HPET_SHARED_IRQ stays set if it was set), leaves hd_irq unchanged and returns -EIO. Otherwise it stores the IRQ in hd_irq and, with local interrupts disabled, ORs 32-bit mode and interrupt-enable into a config value g; for a HPET_PERIODIC device it writes the config with Tn_TYPE_CNF_MASK and Tn_VAL_SET_CNF_MASK set and writes the compare register twice (first value and then the period), for a one-shot device it writes the compare register once; if HPET_SHARED_IRQ is set it clears the timer's ISR bit; then it writes g to the config register, restores interrupts and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (annotation reverses order; final config written before shared ISR clear) is wrong: hpet.c:531-535 clears the ISR bit first and writes the final config (writeq(g)) afterward, which matches the prose order. Original claim (HPET_SHARED_IRQ not restored on request_irq failure) is right (491 toggles only HPET_IE) and was already stated; rewrote with explicit conditions.

name: handle_one_recv_msg
prose: Precondition: intf is a valid IPMI SMI interface and msg is a received SMI message with rsp, rsp_size, data and data_size set. Postcondition: returns 1 when the message must be requeued, 0 when it may be freed, or -1 when it must be neither freed nor requeued (the value comes from the handler that processes the message, or is 0 where the code returns early). The function first screens the message: if rsp_size is below 2, msg->rsp is rewritten into a 3-byte IPMI_ERR_UNSPECIFIED response built from msg->data and processing continues. Otherwise for an IPMB-direct message, a command (response bit clear) with rsp_size below 4 only increments invalid_commands and returns 0, and a response with rsp_size below 5 increments invalid_ipmb_responses, is rewritten to a 5-byte IPMI_ERR_UNSPECIFIED response and processing continues. Otherwise, for a non-IPMB-direct message that is the local SEND_MSG response (data_size at least 2, data[0] the APP request netfn, data[1] IPMI_SEND_MSG_CMD, recv_msg NULL): if intf->in_shutdown or run_to_completion is set it returns 0; else a response code outside {0, node busy, lost arbitration, bus error, NAK on write} counts a sent-command error by channel medium and calls intf_err_seq, other codes call intf_start_seq_timer, and it returns 0. Otherwise a response whose netfn or command does not match the request is rewritten to the 3-byte unspecified-error response and processing continues. It then dispatches: an IPMB-direct message whose request was a response is treated as a response to a response (the recv_msg, if present, is delivered with IPMI_RESPONSE_RESPONSE_TYPE through deliver_local_response and 0 is returned); other IPMB-direct messages go to handle_ipmb_direct_rcv_cmd or handle_ipmb_direct_rcv_rsp; a SEND_MSG response with recv_msg set is delivered as a response to a response unless run_to_completion is set (returns 0); a GET_MSG response returns 0 when run_to_completion is set, the channel is invalid or channels are not ready, and otherwise goes to the IPMB, LAN/async or OEM get-message handlers, with 0 for other channel media; a READ_EVENT_MSG_BUFFER response goes to handle_read_event_rsp unless run_to_completion is set (returns 0); anything else goes to handle_bmc_rsp.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the local SEND_MSG response returns 0 early when in_shutdown or run_to_completion (ipmi_msghandler.c:4632-4633). Round 2 partly right: only an IPMB-direct command with rsp_size < 4 is counted without rewrite (the rsp_size < 2 case is rewritten first, line 4595-4607); the SEND_MSG local-response is not rewritten (right). Original (malformed IPMB command not rewritten) right. Function starts at 4585; slice is partly outside.

name: handle_flags
prose: Precondition: the caller holds ssif_info's message lock (taken through ipmi_ssif_lock_cond, with the saved flags passed by pointer); ssif_info->msg_flags is valid. Postcondition: the function releases the lock through ipmi_ssif_unlock_cond on each branch; one branch temporarily retakes and releases it again. If WDT_PRE_TIMEOUT_INT is set in msg_flags, it increments the watchdog_pretimeouts statistic and calls start_clear_flags, which clears that flag, sets ssif_state to SSIF_CLEARING_FLAGS, unlocks, and sends a clear-message-flags command (ssif_state becomes SSIF_IDLE if start_send fails); then it calls ipmi_smi_watchdog_pretimeout(ssif_info->intf). Otherwise, if RECEIVE_MSG_AVAIL is set, start_recv_msg_fetch allocates an smi message: if allocation fails ssif_state becomes SSIF_IDLE and the lock is released (nothing to free); otherwise curr_msg is set to the message, num_requests_in_a_row is reset to 0 and ssif_state set to SSIF_GETTING_MESSAGES when it was not already that, the lock is released and a get-message command is sent, and if start_send fails check_start_send relocks, clears curr_msg, sets SSIF_IDLE, unlocks and frees the message. Otherwise, if EVENT_MSG_BUFFER_FULL is set, start_event_fetch behaves the same way with req_events cleared first, SSIF_GETTING_EVENTS and a read-event-message-buffer command. Otherwise ssif_state is set to SSIF_IDLE and the lock is released with no command sent.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: allocation failure at ipmi_ssif.c:412-416 / 438-442 sets SSIF_IDLE and returns, no message exists to free. Round 2 (send-failure path in check_start_send relocks and unlocks again) right and stated. Original (omits watchdog pretimeout call and statistic) addressed.

name: write_block
prose: Precondition: p is a byte offset into the flash device, count is nonnegative and buf is a user buffer; the caller holds no lock required by this function. Postcondition: count is clamped to 0x10000 minus (p & 0xFFFF). For each byte it reads the byte from user space with __get_user (return -EFAULT at once if that fails, possibly after earlier bytes were written), programs it, and polls the status for up to one second; if the status wait times out the write is retried for that byte with no deadline on the retries; if the status shows the hardware error bit (0x10) it resets the chip and, if the 30-second deadline taken at entry has not passed, sleeps 10 ms and retries the byte, and otherwise returns -2. After the write loop it sleeps 10 ms and verifies by re-reading each byte from the user buffer and comparing with the flash: a user read failure returns -EFAULT, a mismatch logs an error and returns 0, and when all bytes match it returns the clamped count.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (verify mismatch returns -1, not 0) is wrong: nwflash.c:539-543 returns 0. Round 2 claim (omits -EIO after the 30-second timeout) is wrong in the errno: the code returns -2 (line 524), which the prose already stated. Original (success returns count) right.

name: pc8736x_gpio_init
prose: Precondition: module initialization; no resources of this driver are held. Postcondition: it allocates a platform device (returning -ENOMEM on failure) and adds it (on failure the error is replaced with -ENODEV and only platform_device_put is done). It then returns -ENODEV, after platform_device_del and platform_device_put, if the SuperI/O chip is absent, the chip is not enabled (SIO_CF1 bit 0 clear), or the GPIO unit is not activated; it reads the GPIO base address and returns -ENODEV, after the same cleanup, when request_region fails. It then registers the chardev region (register_chrdev_region when major is nonzero, otherwise alloc_chrdev_region, which also sets major); if that returns a negative value it releases the region, deletes and puts the platform device and returns that negative errno. On success it calls pc8736x_init_shadow, initializes the cdev and calls cdev_add (its result ignored) and returns 0, leaving pdev, major, pc8736x_gpio_base, the ioport region and the chardev region held for pc8736x_gpio_cleanup.
note: Function touches globals, so contract left empty (previous contract was a loose error range). Failure paths checked against pc8736x_gpio.c:259-337: platform_device_add failure jumps to undo_platform_dev_alloc (put only, no del).

name: init_phase
prose: Precondition: mode is any int. Postcondition: the function returns IEEE1284_PH_REV_IDLE when mode with the IEEE1284_DEVICEID and IEEE1284_ADDR bits cleared equals IEEE1284_MODE_NIBBLE (0) or IEEE1284_MODE_BYTE (1), and returns IEEE1284_PH_FWD_IDLE for every other value of mode; it has no other effects.
note: Contract rewritten: IEEE1284_DEVICEID is 1<<2 (4) and IEEE1284_ADDR is 1<<13 (8192), so the cleared mask is 8196 (the old contract used ~12), and IEEE1284_PH_FWD_IDLE is enum value 1 and IEEE1284_PH_REV_IDLE is 5 (parport.h:163-169), not 0 and 5.

name: pp_do_ioctl
prose: Precondition: file is an open ppdev file whose private_data points to a valid struct pp_struct for iminor(file_inode(file)), and arg points to user memory of the size the command copies (a byte for PPRSTATUS, PPRDATA, PPRCONTROL, PPWCONTROL, PPWDATA and PPWCTLONIRQ, two bytes for PPFCONTROL, an int for PPSETMODE, PPGETMODE, PPSETPHASE, PPGETPHASE, PPSETFLAGS, PPGETFLAGS, PPDATADIR, PPNEGOT and PPCLRIRQ, an unsigned int for PPGETMODES, two 32-bit or two 64-bit values for the time commands). Postcondition: it returns 0 after the command or a negative errno. PPCLAIM returns -EINVAL if PP_CLAIMED is set; if pp->pdev is NULL it first calls register_device, returning its error (-ENOMEM from kasprintf, -ENXIO when no port or parport_register_dev_model fails, or the ida_alloc error such as -ENOMEM or -ENOSPC) with pdev left unset; it then calls parport_claim_or_block and returns its negative error (for example -EINTR) with PP_CLAIMED unset and a newly registered pdev left registered; on success it sets PP_CLAIMED, enables interrupts, saves the port's ieee1284 mode and phase in saved_state, installs pp->state's mode and phase, reads the default inactivity timeout and sets it back, and returns 0. PPEXCL returns 0 and sets PP_EXCL when pdev is NULL, returns 0 when pdev is set and PP_EXCL is already set, and returns -EINVAL when pdev is set without PP_EXCL. PPSETMODE and PPSETPHASE copy an int from user space (-EFAULT on failure), store it in pp->state (PPSETMODE also sets the phase from init_phase) and, when claimed, in the port's ieee1284 state, and return 0. PPGETMODE, PPGETPHASE, PPGETFLAGS and PPGETMODES copy a value to user space and return 0 or -EFAULT; PPGETMODES returns -ENODEV when no port exists for the minor and releases the temporary port reference with parport_put_port. PPSETFLAGS copies an int (-EFAULT on failure), replaces the PP_FLAGMASK bits of pp->flags and returns 0. Any other command returns -EINVAL if PP_CLAIMED is clear. When claimed: PPRSTATUS, PPRDATA and PPRCONTROL read a byte and copy it out (-EFAULT on failure); PPYIELD yields the port; PPRELEASE saves the port's mode and phase into pp->state, restores saved_state to the port, releases the port and clears PP_CLAIMED; PPWCONTROL, PPWDATA, PPFCONTROL, PPDATADIR copy from user space (-EFAULT on failure) and write the register, frob the control lines or set the data direction; PPNEGOT copies an int, calls parport_negotiate, maps -1 to -EIO and 1 to -ENXIO, calls pp_enable_irq and returns the result; PPWCTLONIRQ copies a byte (-EFAULT on failure), stores it in irqctl and sets irqresponse to 1; PPCLRIRQ copies irqc out as an int (-EFAULT on failure, irqc then not reduced) and subtracts it from irqc; PPSETTIME32 and PPSETTIME64 copy two values (-EFAULT on failure), return -EINVAL for a negative value and otherwise return pp_set_timeout, which fails with -EINVAL when the microseconds are at least USEC_PER_SEC or the converted timeout is not positive (PPSETTIME64 shifts the microsecond field right by 32 on sparc64 non-compat); PPGETTIME32 and PPGETTIME64 convert pdev->timeout to seconds and microseconds and copy them out (-EFAULT on failure; PPGETTIME64 shifts left by 32 on sparc64 non-compat); any other command returns -EINVAL.
note: Checked against ppdev.c:361-674. Corrected pp_set_timeout wording (to_jiffies <= 0, line 354) and dropped the unqualified 'no command partially updates state' claim. Reviewer claims (register_device errors include ida_alloc error and -ENOSPC; pdev left registered on claim failure) are right and reflected.

name: wait_for_stat
prose: Precondition: chip is a valid tpm_chip whose device drvdata is a struct st33zp24_dev; queue is a valid wait queue; chip->ops->status (and chip->ops->req_canceled when check_cancel is true) are callable. Postcondition: it returns 0 if the status read at entry has all bits of mask set. Otherwise with the IRQ flag clear it loops msleep(TPM_TIMEOUT) then reads the status and returns 0 as soon as all mask bits are set, and returns -ETIME when time_before(jiffies, stop) becomes false; check_cancel is not used on this path. With TPM_CHIP_FLAG_IRQ set it clears the pending interrupt, enables tpm_dev->irq and loops: when -ERESTARTSYS was returned and the thread is freezing it clears TIF_SIGPENDING; if the time to the deadline is not positive it returns -1 (irq left enabled); otherwise it waits with wait_event_interruptible_timeout, clears the interrupt again, and evaluates the condition that the status has all mask bits set or, with check_cancel true, req_canceled reports cancellation. If the wait returned a non-negative value and the condition holds it returns -ECANCELED when the cancel branch caused it (status did not have the mask) and otherwise 0, in both cases without disabling the irq. The loop repeats only while the wait returned -ERESTARTSYS and the thread is freezing; any other exit calls disable_irq_nosync and returns -ETIME.
note: Reviewer round 15 claim (non-IRQ path returning -ECANCELED) is wrong: st33zp24.c:253-260 uses chip->ops->status only and never check_cancel; -ETIME is the non-IRQ timeout. Round 2 (IRQ path returns 0 or -ECANCELED inside the loop without disable_irq_nosync) right and stated; original (omits -ETIME on non-IRQ timeout) addressed.
